There are many good ideas here. One that I have not seen so far is what I call adopting the "Zen of Travel". Airline travel can be very unpredictable with maintenance, weather, crew issues, etc. Adopt the attitude that you will get there when you get there, that delays happen. The only thing in your control is how you handle it. When a delay happens, don't freak out, and don't get angry. If you need to deal with airline personnel to rectify an issue, you will do yourself a huge favor if you are in a decent mood, calm and respectful. I have personally been in situations where simply being kind and patient with an airline customer service rep opened up opportunities that got me home earlier than I would have otherwise. These are people that get yelled at a lot - you will most always have better results by being nice.

My standard flight kit includes:
* Earplugs and/or quality noise-isolating earbuds - long term exposure to noise is more tiring than you realize
* An empty water bottle that I fill up after I'm through "security" - low air pressure + low humidity is very dehydrating so make sure you drink water on longer flights
* Tablet with ebooks and lots of music
